messages:
ana: quick sync — background job svc keys vs project-bound keys are causing authz mismatches this morning. job `ingest-cleanup` running under svc-key gets rejected for project-level resource access.
vikram: saw that. root cause: svc key lacks org/project claim. jobs used to run as 'service' actor, but new RBAC checks require `project:<id>` in token.
maria: what's current behavior for the proxy? does it synthesize project claim from svc->project mapping?
ana: proxy currently maps if token is project-bound, otherwise treats as org service. no synth.
vikram: options: 1) keep current and widen service roles (not ideal). 2) synth claims in proxy from metadata mapping (risky, implicit elevation). 3) require ephemeral project-scoped tokens for jobs (correct long-term but heavy migration).
josh: +1 on ephemeral project-scoped tokens. least privilege wins. migration pain is real though for large fleets.
ana: short-term proposal from infra: add an explicit mapping table in AuthN (svc_id -> allowed project_ids). Auth service can assert a project claim when mapped and when request comes from a verified internal job queue. Precedence rule: explicit project-bound token > asserted mapping > plain service token.
maria: can we gate assertion per-tenant with a feature flag? we shouldn't open blanket implicit claims.
vikram: yep — feature flag per-org + audit logs. also emit a trace header `X-Auth-Decision: mapped-project` so downstream teams can find these requests.
dev-bot: PR checklist suggestion:
```
- DB migration: service_project_mappings
- New admin endpoint: POST /admin/mappings
- Feature flag: auth.assert_mapped_projects
- Logging: audit_entry with actor, svc_id, mapped_project_id
```
josh: quick test command we can use after a mapping is created:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer svc-XXXX" https://api.redwood.ai/projects/123/resource
# expect 200 with header X-Auth-Decision: mapped-project
```
nana: long-term: RFC "unify-service-auth-around-scoped-claims" — move all jobs to short-lived project-scoped tokens minted by broker (via workload identity). timeline ~3 months. migration path: dual-accept mode (tokens + mapped assertions) for 6 weeks, then flip.
maria: i'll draft the mapping schema + admin UI wireframe. sketch for mapping record:
```
{
  "svc_id": "svc-ingest-01",
  "allowed_projects": ["proj-123", "proj-456"],
  "reason": "ingest jobs owned by data-platform",
  "expires_at": null
}
```
vikram: also add TTL and rotation recommendations. we should rotate mapping assertions every 30d as part of hygiene.
sre-bot: note: alert rule to detect any `mapped-project` decisions with >1% of failed authorizations in past hour.
josh: should we add an explicit acceptance test to the CI harness that simulates project revocation? to ensure mappings are respected.
nana: good idea. action items: @maria owns mapping API + UI, @vikram owns auth service change + trace header, @ana owns RFC draft and migration plan, @josh owns CI tests/canary. i'll create the initial tickets and a tiny PR tomorrow to add the DB migration + feature flag. :thumbsup: 
vikram: i'll set up a canary stack and load a small job backlog to exercise case. will post metrics in #eng-sre.
maria: ack, starting draft now.
nana: if no objections, proceed. low-risk, auditable, and buys time for the broker migration. thanks all.
